name: Gmail
description: Let your AI work in Gmail: search the mailbox with Gmail's own search syntax, read messages and conversations, see labels and unread counts, mark mail as read, archive, star or label it, and send the drafts you wrote. Personal Gmail and Google Workspace, signed in with your Google account.
instructions:
## Gmail
This connector reads and organises the signed-in user's Gmail mailbox through the **Gmail API v1** (`https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me`). It works with personal Gmail accounts and with Google Workspace mailboxes. Everything runs as the Google account that authorized the connector: the AI sees exactly what that account can see.

**Setup (one-time, about 10 minutes)**
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com, pick or create a project, then **APIs & Services → Library** → enable **Gmail API**.
2. **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**: choose **Internal** if the mailbox is on Google Workspace (simplest, see *Google verification* below), otherwise **External**. For External, set the publishing status to **In production**: while an app is in *Testing*, Google revokes its refresh tokens after 7 days and the connector stops working every week.
3. **APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID** → application type **Web application** → add the authorized redirect URI `<your AnythingMCP URL>/api/mcp-oauth/callback` (on AnythingMCP Cloud: `https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/api/mcp-oauth/callback`).
4. Paste the client ID and secret into `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and install the connector.
5. On the connector page, click **Authorize with Provider** and sign in with the Gmail account the AI should work with. The refresh token is stored encrypted and access tokens are renewed automatically.

**Google verification (restricted scopes)**: Google classifies `gmail.modify` and `gmail.readonly` as *restricted* scopes. An **External** app that other people use needs Google's OAuth app verification, which for restricted scopes includes a security assessment; until then Google shows a "Google hasn't verified this app" warning and caps the app at 100 users. An **Internal** app, used only by accounts of the Google Workspace organisation that owns the Cloud project, needs no verification: it is the straightforward route for a company. For a single personal Gmail account, an External app *In production* that only you use works after you continue past the warning.

**Scope**: the connector asks for `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`: read mail, change labels (mark read, archive, star) and send drafts. It cannot permanently delete anything. For a read-only setup, change the scope to `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly` in the connector's OAuth settings, authorize again, and disable `gmail_modify_message_labels`, `gmail_modify_thread_labels` and `gmail_send_draft`.

**Finding mail**: `gmail_list_messages` and `gmail_list_threads` take `q` in the same syntax as the Gmail search box, e.g. `from:ana@example.com`, `is:unread`, `newer_than:7d`, `after:2026/10/01 before:2026/10/08`, `has:attachment`, `subject:offer`, `label:invoices`, `in:inbox`, `-category:promotions`. They return ids only (messages: `id` and `threadId`; threads: `id`, `snippet`, `historyId`); fetch the content with `gmail_get_message` or `gmail_get_thread`. `label_ids` filters on labels that must all be present.

**Reading a message**
- `format: "metadata"` with `metadata_headers` (e.g. `["From", "To", "Subject", "Date"]`) returns the headers, labels and `snippet` only. It is the cheapest way to triage many messages.
- `format: "full"` (the default) returns `payload`, the parsed MIME tree: `payload.headers`, then `parts[]` with a `mimeType` (`text/plain`, `text/html`, `multipart/alternative`, …), nested `parts` for multipart containers, and `body.data`.
- **`body.data` is base64url-encoded** (URL-safe alphabet with `-` and `_`, padding often missing), as Gmail returns it; this connector does not decode it. Read the `text/plain` part when there is one. `snippet` is a short plain-text excerpt that needs no decoding.
- Attachments appear as parts with a `filename` and a `body.attachmentId`; this connector does not download them.
- `format: "minimal"` returns only ids and labels; `raw` returns the whole message as one base64url string and is rarely useful here.

**Labels**: system labels have fixed ids: `INBOX`, `UNREAD`, `STARRED`, `IMPORTANT`, `SENT`, `DRAFT`, `SPAM`, `TRASH`, `CATEGORY_PERSONAL`, `CATEGORY_SOCIAL`, `CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS`, `CATEGORY_UPDATES`, `CATEGORY_FORUMS`. User labels have ids such as `Label_12`: take them from `gmail_list_labels`, not from the label name. `gmail_get_label` adds the message and unread counts. With `gmail_modify_message_labels` / `gmail_modify_thread_labels`: mark as read = remove `UNREAD`; mark as unread = add `UNREAD`; archive = remove `INBOX`; star = add `STARRED`; file = add the label id (and remove `INBOX` to move it out of the inbox). Up to 100 label ids per call.

**Drafts and sending**: `gmail_list_drafts` and `gmail_get_draft` read the drafts in the mailbox, and `gmail_send_draft` sends one exactly as it was written; Gmail then removes the draft and the message gets the `SENT` label. This connector does not compose new messages or replies: Gmail only accepts a complete RFC 822 message for that, and the connector does not build one.

**Pagination**: list responses carry `nextPageToken` while more results exist; call the same tool again with the same arguments and `page_token` set to it. `max_results` goes up to 500 (default 100). `resultSizeEstimate` is an estimate, not an exact count.

**Rate limits**: Gmail meters quota units: 6,000 per minute per user and 1,200,000 per minute per project. A list costs 5 units, `gmail_get_message` 20, `gmail_get_thread` 40, a label change 5 (10 on a thread), sending a draft 100, the profile and labels 1. Over the limit Gmail answers 429 (or 403 `userRateLimitExceeded`): wait a minute and retry. One message reaches at most 500 recipients.

**Common errors**
- 401: the authorization expired or was revoked (always after 7 days while the consent screen is in *Testing*). Click **Authorize with Provider** again.
- 403 `insufficientPermissions` / `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`: the scope does not allow the call, e.g. a label change on a read-only setup. 403 `accessNotConfigured` / "Gmail API has not been used in project": enable the Gmail API in the Cloud project (step 1).
- 404: the id does not exist in this mailbox, or the message was deleted. A draft id (`r-…`) is not a message id.
- 400 `invalidArgument`: a label id that does not exist, or an invalid query parameter.

**Out of scope here**: composing new messages and replies, attachments, trash and deletion, filters, settings, other users' mailboxes.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.label: OAuth client ID
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.help: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials → your OAuth client of type Web application.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.patternMessage: A Google OAuth client ID ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.label: OAuth client secret
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.help: The client secret of the same OAuth client.

verifyHints.401: Google refused the access token. Click Authorize with Provider again; if the OAuth consent screen is still in Testing, set it to In production first, otherwise the authorization expires after 7 days.
verifyHints.403: The Gmail API is not enabled in the Google Cloud project, or the authorized scope does not allow this call. Enable the Gmail API under APIs & Services → Library and authorize again.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Gmail is throttling this mailbox (6,000 quota units per minute per user). Wait a minute and try again.

prerequisites: A Google Cloud project with the **Gmail API** enabled, an OAuth consent screen (**Internal** on Google Workspace, or External set to *In production*) and a Web OAuth client with the redirect URI below. Gmail scopes are restricted: outside a single Workspace organisation, Google shows an unverified-app warning until the app passes its verification. About 10 minutes.

tools.name: gmail_get_profile
tools.description: Return the Gmail account the connector works with: its email address, the total number of messages and threads in the mailbox, and the current history id.

tools.name: gmail_list_messages
tools.description: Search or list messages in the mailbox with Gmail search syntax and optional label filters. Returns message ids and thread ids (no content), nextPageToken while more results exist, and an estimated total; read a message with gmail_get_message.

q.description: Gmail search query, same syntax as the Gmail search box, e.g. "from:ana@example.com is:unread newer_than:7d" or "subject:invoice has:attachment".

label_ids.description: Only messages that carry all of these label ids, e.g. ["INBOX", "UNREAD"]. User label ids come from gmail_list_labels.

max_results.description: Maximum number of messages per page, 1 to 500 (default 100).

page_token.description: nextPageToken from the previous response, to fetch the next page with the same other arguments.

include_spam_trash.description: true to include messages in Spam and Trash (default false).

tools.name: gmail_get_message
tools.description: Get one message by id: labels, snippet, internal date and, depending on format, the headers (From, To, Cc, Subject, Date) and the MIME payload whose body parts are base64url-encoded as Gmail returns them.

message_id.description: Message id from gmail_list_messages or gmail_get_thread.

format.description: How much of the message to return: "full" (default) parsed MIME payload with headers and base64url-encoded body parts; "metadata" headers, labels and snippet only; "minimal" ids and labels only; "raw" the whole RFC 822 message as one base64url string.

metadata_headers.description: With format "metadata": only these headers, e.g. ["From", "To", "Subject", "Date"].

tools.name: gmail_list_threads
tools.description: Search or list conversations (threads) with Gmail search syntax and optional label filters. Returns thread ids with a snippet and history id, nextPageToken while more results exist, and an estimated total; read a thread's messages with gmail_get_thread.

q.description: Gmail search query, same syntax as the Gmail search box, e.g. "from:ana@example.com is:unread newer_than:7d" or "subject:invoice has:attachment".

label_ids.description: Only threads that carry all of these label ids, e.g. ["INBOX", "UNREAD"]. User label ids come from gmail_list_labels.

max_results.description: Maximum number of threads per page, 1 to 500 (default 100).

page_token.description: nextPageToken from the previous response, to fetch the next page with the same other arguments.

include_spam_trash.description: true to include threads in Spam and Trash (default false).

tools.name: gmail_get_thread
tools.description: Get one conversation by thread id with all its messages in order. Each message has the same shape as in gmail_get_message for the chosen format.

thread_id.description: Thread id from gmail_list_threads or the threadId of a message.

format.description: How much of the messages to return: "full" (default) parsed MIME payload with headers and base64url-encoded body parts; "metadata" headers, labels and snippet only; "minimal" ids and labels only.

metadata_headers.description: With format "metadata": only these headers, e.g. ["From", "To", "Subject", "Date"].

tools.name: gmail_list_labels
tools.description: List all labels of the mailbox, system labels (INBOX, UNREAD, STARRED, SENT, SPAM, TRASH, categories) and the user's own, with id, name and type. Label ids are what the search filters and the label tools take.

tools.name: gmail_get_label
tools.description: Get one label by id with its message and thread counts, total and unread, plus its visibility settings and colour.

label_id.description: Label id, e.g. INBOX, UNREAD or Label_12 from gmail_list_labels.

tools.name: gmail_modify_message_labels
tools.description: Add and remove labels on one message: mark it read (remove UNREAD) or unread (add UNREAD), archive it (remove INBOX), star it (add STARRED) or file it under a user label. Returns the message's id, thread id and resulting labels.

add_label_ids.description: Label ids to add, e.g. ["STARRED"] or ["Label_12"]. Up to 100.

remove_label_ids.description: Label ids to remove, e.g. ["UNREAD"] to mark as read or ["INBOX"] to archive. Up to 100.

tools.name: gmail_modify_thread_labels
tools.description: Add and remove labels on every message of a conversation at once, e.g. archive a whole thread (remove INBOX) or mark it read (remove UNREAD). Returns the thread with its messages' ids and labels.

add_label_ids.description: Label ids to add to all messages of the thread. Up to 100.

remove_label_ids.description: Label ids to remove from all messages of the thread. Up to 100.

tools.name: gmail_list_drafts
tools.description: List the drafts in the mailbox, optionally filtered with Gmail search syntax. Returns each draft's id with its message id and thread id, and nextPageToken while more exist; read one with gmail_get_draft.

q.description: Gmail search query applied to the drafts, e.g. "to:ana@example.com" or "subject:offer".

max_results.description: Maximum number of drafts per page, 1 to 500 (default 100).

include_spam_trash.description: true to include drafts in Spam and Trash (default false).

tools.name: gmail_get_draft
tools.description: Get one draft by draft id with its message: recipients, subject and body in the chosen format, to check it before it is sent.

draft_id.description: Draft id (it starts with r-) from gmail_list_drafts; not a message id.

format.description: How much of the draft to return: "full" (default) parsed MIME payload with headers and base64url-encoded body parts; "metadata" headers, labels and snippet only; "minimal" ids and labels only; "raw" the whole RFC 822 message as one base64url string.

tools.name: gmail_send_draft
tools.description: Send an existing draft to its recipients exactly as it is written. Gmail removes the draft and returns the sent message with its id, thread id and the SENT label.
